title: Best AI Homework Helpers in 2026 (That Teach You, Not Only Answer)
summary: 14 AI homework helpers for 2026 compared on vendor pages: math, science and essays, free tiers, study modes, and when AI help builds or removes the skill.
body_markdown:
Po-Shen Loh coached the United States team at the International Mathematical Olympiad for a decade. In a 2025 interview, he put the whole problem of AI homework into two sentences:


> "People used to go to school to learn how to do the homework and do the exams. Today, everyone needs to learn how to grade the homework."


He is not telling students to stop doing homework. He is telling them that the answer is now cheap, and the judgment about the answer is not. An AI homework helper can produce a clean solution to almost any school problem in seconds. The open question is whether you walk away from that session able to do the next one yourself, and able to spot when the AI got it wrong.


That is the difference this guide is built around. Some AI homework helpers give you the answer. Others build the skill. Most can do both, and the setting you choose, the order you work in, and the prompt you type decide which one you get.


> **TL;DR:** We compared **14 AI homework helpers** from vendor pages in November 2026.[Photomath](https://photomath.com/) and[Wolfram Alpha](https://www.wolframalpha.com/) lead for math steps.[ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/) study mode and[Khanmigo](https://www.khanmigo.ai/) lead for learning instead of answers. ## Answer Helper vs Skill Helper: The Difference That Decides Your Grade


**An answer helper gives you the solution to this problem. A skill helper leaves you able to solve the next problem without it.** Both can be useful. The trouble starts when a student uses an answer helper for practice that exists to build a skill, because the practice was the point.


Po-Shen Loh has a sharp analogy for this. He compares using AI for homework to driving "my car one mile for exercise." The car works. You arrive. But the mile was never about arriving. It was about the walk. An adult who already has a skill can delegate the task and lose nothing. A student who is still building that skill loses the exercise the homework was designed to give.


Loh's wider point is about judgment. In the same interview he warns that AI "is going to be so good at looking complete that you may think you have the entire story." A student who can only copy an AI solution cannot tell when that solution is wrong. A student who did the work can. That is what "grade the homework" means in practice: you need the skill first, so that you can judge the machine's output later. We cover his full argument in[skills AI can't replace](https://www.taskade.com/blog/skills-ai-cant-replace) .


Answer helper Skill helper

## What the Research Says About AI and Homework


**The strongest evidence so far shows that the same AI can help or harm learning, and the design of the help decides which.** A 2025 randomized trial in *PNAS* found that a plain chatbot raised practice scores but lowered later exam scores, while a hint-giving tutor version raised practice scores with no exam loss.


That study, led by Hamsa Bastani of the Wharton School, ran in a high school in Turkey with nearly 1,000 students. One group practiced math with a standard GPT-4 chat interface ("GPT Base"). A second group used a version with teacher-designed prompts that gave hints and held back the full answer ("GPT Tutor"). A third group had no AI.


Group Practice sessions vs no-AI group Later exam without AI vs no-AI group


GPT Base (plain chatbot) 48 percent higher 17 percent lower


GPT Tutor (hints, no direct answers) 127 percent higher No significant difference


No AI Baseline Baseline


The authors' reading: students used the plain chatbot as a crutch during practice, then performed worse on their own. The guardrails in the tutor version protected learning. That one table is the clearest evidence for Loh's car analogy we know of.


### The Learning Science Behind "Attempt First"


The Bastani result matches decades of research on how memory and skill form. None of these studies is about AI. All of them explain why answer-first help feels productive and still fails on the test.


Effect Primary study What it shows What it means for AI homework


Testing effect Roediger and Karpicke, 2006, *Psychological Science* Recalling material beats re-reading it on delayed tests, even though re-readers feel more confident Ask AI to quiz you, not to explain again


Generation effect Slamecka and Graf, 1978, *Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Learning and Memory* Information you produce yourself is remembered better than information you read Write your own attempt before you read a solution


Self-explanation Chi, Bassok, Lewis, Reimann and Glaser, 1989, *Cognitive Science* Strong learners explain worked examples to themselves, weak learners do not After any AI solution, explain each step in your own words


Failed attempts help Kornell, Hays and Bjork, 2009, *Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition* Trying to answer before you know improves later learning, even when the try fails A wrong attempt before the hint is not wasted


Productive failure Kapur, 2008, *Cognition and Instruction* Struggling with a problem before instruction can improve understanding Some struggle is the learning, not a bug


Worked examples Sweller and Cooper, 1985, *Cognition and Instruction* Beginners learn algebra faster from studying worked examples than from solving alone A solved example is fine early, if you then solve a fresh one


Expertise reversal Kalyuga, Ayres, Chandler and Sweller, 2003, *Educational Psychologist* Support that helps beginners can slow down more skilled learners Step down the help as you improve


Desirable difficulties Bjork and Bjork, 2011, in *Psychology and the Real World* Conditions that slow learning, such as retrieval and spacing, build stronger long-term memory Effort during practice is a feature


Illusion of explanatory depth Rozenblit and Keil, 2002, *Cognitive Science* People overrate how well they understand until they try to explain Reading an AI explanation feels like understanding it


Study technique review Dunlosky and colleagues, 2013, *Psychological Science in the Public Interest* Practice testing and spaced practice rank as the highest-utility study techniques Pair AI help with self-testing and[spaced repetition](https://www.taskade.com/blog/spaced-repetition-explained)


Two rows deserve a second look because they push against a simple "never look at the answer" rule. The worked-example effect says beginners can learn a lot from studying a full solution. The expertise reversal effect says that same support becomes a drag once you know the basics. So the honest rule is not "never see a solution." It is "see a solution, explain it, then solve a fresh problem alone, and ask for less help each week."


### Cognitive Offloading: Why It Feels Fine Until the Test


**Cognitive offloading is the habit of moving mental work onto a tool, and people choose it when they believe the tool is more reliable than their own memory or reasoning.** Evan Risko and Sam Gilbert defined the term in a 2016 review in *Trends in Cognitive Sciences* . Offloading is often smart. A calculator for arithmetic in a physics class frees attention for the physics.


The problem is offloading the exact skill the homework is training. A 2025 study by Hao-Ping Lee and colleagues at Microsoft Research and Carnegie Mellon, presented at CHI 2025, surveyed 319 knowledge workers about 936 real uses of generative AI. Workers who trusted the AI more reported less critical thinking, and their effort moved toward checking, combining and managing AI output. That shift is fine for an adult who already has the skill. For a student, it skips the stage where the skill forms. We explain the concept in depth in[what is cognitive offloading](https://www.taskade.com/blog/cognitive-offloading) .


### Students Already Delegate the Hard Parts


**Students use AI for homework at scale, and much of that use hands over the answer, not the learning.** Pew Research Center found that 26 percent of US teens ages 13 to 17 used ChatGPT for schoolwork in a fall 2024 survey of 1,391 teens, double the 13 percent in 2023. Anthropic's April 2025 education report found that about 47 percent of student conversations with Claude were "direct" requests for answers or content with little back-and-forth.


Teens themselves draw a line. In the same Pew survey, far more teens said it was acceptable to use ChatGPT to research new topics than to solve math problems or write essays.


That instinct is close to the research. Using AI to find and explain is low risk. Using AI to do the math or write the essay removes the practice the task was built to give.


### A Well-Built AI Can Teach


**AI is not the enemy of learning. Answer-first AI is.** In a 2025 randomized trial published in *Scientific Reports* , Gregory Kestin and colleagues gave 194 Harvard physics students an AI tutor built on the same teaching practices as an active-learning class. Students using the AI tutor learned more than twice as much, measured against their pre-test, in less time.


The tutor in that study was purpose-built. It asked questions, gave feedback and paced the material. A general chatbot with no guardrails is not the same tool. That is why the learning modes covered below matter, and why the way you prompt any AI helper matters even more. For a deeper look at tutor products, read our guide to[AI tutors](https://www.taskade.com/blog/best-ai-tutors) .

## When Is AI Homework Help Fine, and When Does It Remove the Learning?


**AI homework help is fine when it supports a skill you already own or coaches a skill you are building after your own attempt. It removes the learning when it does the exact skill the homework exists to train.** Your teacher's policy comes first. If an assignment bans AI, no use is fine.


We call the simple version **the Exercise Test** , after Loh's car analogy. Before you open an AI helper, answer three questions:


1. **Is this the skill the homework trains?** If the assignment is "factor these quadratics," factoring is the exercise. If the assignment is a physics lab write-up, checking your unit conversions is not the exercise.
2. **Did I attempt it first, in writing?** A real attempt means at least one line of work, not a glance at the problem.
3. **Can I redo it tomorrow with no AI?** If not, you used an answer helper, whatever the app calls itself.


Three yes answers mean you used AI as a coach. A "no" on the first question means the task is support work, and AI help is usually fine within the rules.


Use of AI Exercise Test result Usually


Explain a concept you got wrong, after your attempt Coach Fine


Check your finished answer against a solver Coach Fine


Generate fresh practice problems on a topic Coach Fine


Quiz you from your own class notes Coach Fine


Build a study schedule before a test Support task Fine


Explain the instructions of an assignment in simpler words Support task Fine


Feedback on grammar in a draft you wrote Depends on the course Check the policy


Outline ideas for an essay Depends on the course Check the policy


Photograph a graded problem set and copy the steps Replaces the exercise Not fine


Have AI write an essay or lab report you submit Replaces the exercise and misstates authorship Not fine


Use AI during a closed test or quiz Breaks the test rules Not fine


The state diagram is the healthy loop. Notice what is missing: there is no path from "Stuck" straight to "Check." Skipping the attempt is the one move that turns a skill helper into an answer helper.

## Math Solvers and Answer Engines


These tools take a problem, often from a photo, and return an answer with steps. They are the fastest checkers you can find. Used before your own attempt, they are also the fastest way to skip the exercise.


### 1. Photomath: Best for Math Steps From a Photo


**[Photomath](https://photomath.com/) is a math app that scans a printed or handwritten problem, including word problems, and shows the solution step by step, sometimes with more than one method.** Google acquired Photomath in 2023 after EU approval, and the app still runs as its own product alongside Google Lens math help.


Photomath's own page says it "is designed for learning," and that framing is fair. Each step appears on its own, with "how" and "why" tips and visual aids, so a student can see where their method went off track. The page lists elementary math, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, statistics and calculus, "for elementary through college."


**Pricing:** The Photomath page lists a Basic plan at $0, a monthly plan at $9.99, and an annual plan at $69.99 labeled "Best Value," each paid plan with a trial button. The page lists the same headline features beside every option, so it does not show exactly what the free plan leaves out.


**Strengths:**


- Fast, clear step view that suits checking a finished problem
- Multiple solution methods on some problems, which helps when your class taught a different approach
- Handles word problems, not only equations


**Watch-outs:** Photomath is math only. A photo scan makes it very easy to skip your own attempt, because the answer is one tap away. If your teacher wants a specific method, the app's first method may not match.


**Skill-safe setting:** Solve the problem on paper first. Then scan it, and compare your steps with Photomath's line by line. Where they differ, write one sentence on why. That turns a solver into a self-explanation exercise, the effect Chi and colleagues measured in 1989.

Subjects Math


Input Camera scan or typed calculator


Teaching style Step-by-step explanations, answer visible

### 2. Mathway: Best for Fast Answers Across Math and Some Science


**[Mathway](https://www.mathway.com/) is an AI-powered math solver and calculator that takes a typed problem or a photo and shows the method, from basic math through calculus, statistics, chemistry and physics.** The footer of its site credits Chegg Inc., so Mathway sits in the same company as Chegg Study.


Mathway's page lists 11 subjects, which makes it wider than most math-only apps. It answers a common question directly: "Yes, Mathway is free to use. You can get step-by-step solutions to math problems without signing up." It adds that "an optional subscription unlocks the full work shown for every step."


**Pricing:** The Mathway page mentions only an optional subscription and an Upgrade link. It did not show a price when we checked, so we print none.


**Strengths:**


- No sign-up needed for basic steps, which makes it quick for a one-off check
- Broad subject menu, including chemistry and physics topics that pure algebra apps skip
- Clean calculator-style input for students who prefer typing to scanning


**Watch-outs:** Mathway is built around getting to an answer quickly. It does not ask you questions or give a hint before the solution, so the teaching depends entirely on how you use it. The full work for every step sits behind the subscription.


**Skill-safe setting:** Use Mathway as a final checker. Cover the steps, compare only your final answer, and look at the steps only if your answer differs. If you need the steps, explain them back in writing before you move on.

Input Typed or photo

### 3. Symbolab: Best for Structured Steps and Hint-Based Practice


**[Symbolab](https://www.symbolab.com/) is an AI math solver, owned by Learneo, Inc., that breaks problems down step by step from pre-algebra through calculus, trigonometry, physics and statistics.** It also offers practice problems with hints, quizzes with feedback, notebooks and a chat assistant called Symbo.


Symbolab stands out from the photo apps because of its practice side. Its page invites students to "explore a wide range of examples, supported by hints." That is closer to the skill-helper model: you solve, and the hint arrives only when you ask for it. The step explanations aim to show why each step follows the last, not only what it is.


**Pricing:** The Symbolab page shows an "Upgrade to Pro" link but did not list a Pro price or say which features are free when we checked. We print no number.


**Strengths:**


- Practice problems with hints, which fit the attempt-first method
- Step explanations that focus on why a step follows
- Accepts typed notation, plain-language requests, and a photo from a notebook


**Watch-outs:** The step-by-step solver is still one paste away from the full answer. Students who only use the solver and never open the practice side get the same risk as any other answer engine.


**Skill-safe setting:** Spend most of your Symbolab time in the practice problems, not the solver. Ask for a hint only after a written attempt. Use the solver to check a problem set after you finish it, never to start one. For a full comparison of math tutoring tools, see[AI math tutoring](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-math-tutoring) .


Symbolab at a glance


Subjects Pre-algebra to calculus, physics, statistics


Input Typed, plain language, or photo


Teaching style Steps, plus practice with hints


Paid price Not shown on vendor page


### 4. Wolfram Alpha: Best for Advanced STEM and Exact Computation


**[Wolfram Alpha](https://www.wolframalpha.com/) is a computational knowledge engine that answers math, science and data questions by computing them, and its Pro plans add step-by-step solutions and practice problems with hints.** It is a favorite for high school and college students in calculus, statistics, physics and chemistry.


What makes Wolfram Alpha different from a chatbot is that it computes. For an integral, a unit conversion or a statistics question, it runs the math rather than predicting text, which makes it a strong checker for numeric answers. The Pro page also describes the Wolfram Problem Generator, which creates fresh practice problems with immediate feedback.


**Pricing:** On the Wolfram Alpha Pro for Students page, Pro is $5.00 per month billed $60.00 annually, and Pro Premium is $8.25 per month billed $99.00 annually. The page states that the free Basic plan "does not include step-by-step solutions."


**Strengths:**


- Computed answers for exact math and science checks
- Practice problems with hints on Pro, a good fit for attempt-first study
- Student pricing that is among the lowest yearly costs on this list


**Watch-outs:** Wolfram Alpha is powerful but formal. Younger students can find its input style and output hard to read, and the steps are a paid feature. For an essay or history question, it is the wrong tool.


**Skill-safe setting:** Use the free Basic plan to check your final numeric answer. If you are wrong, try once more before you look at Pro steps. Use the Problem Generator to practice the exact skill you missed.

Subjects Math, science, data, units


Input Typed, natural language or math notation


Teaching style Computed answers, steps and practice on Pro


Paid price Students: $5/month billed $60/year


### 5. Gauth: Best for Help Across Many Subjects on a Phone


**[Gauth](https://www.gauthmath.com/) is a homework app, published by GauthTech Pte. Ltd., that answers questions in math, biology, physics, chemistry and other subjects, and adds a voice-based AI Live Tutor and access to human subject experts.** Its App Store listing calls it "Gauth: AI Study Companion."


Gauth is wide. Where Photomath stays in math, Gauth takes a photo of a chemistry question or a biology diagram too. Its AI Live Tutor talks through a problem by voice with a virtual whiteboard, and the app offers "round-the-clock access to a global network of subject matter experts" when the AI is not enough.


**Pricing:** The US App Store lists Gauth PLUS at $11.99 per month, $31.99 per quarter, or $99.99 per year, and notes that "prices may vary by region." The in-app purchase list also shows trial and special-offer entries, so read the exact offer on screen before you start a trial.


**Strengths:**


- One app for many subjects, not only math
- A voice tutor with a whiteboard, which suits students who learn by talking
- Human experts as a backup for problems the AI misreads


**Watch-outs:** Gauth's main path is photo to answer, which makes it easy to skip your attempt. Several trial and discount entries in the purchase list mean parents should check the renewal terms. Check your school device rules before you install it.


**Skill-safe setting:** Use the AI Live Tutor instead of the instant answer, and tell it at the start: "Do not give me the answer. Ask me what I think the first step is." That small instruction turns a solver into a coach.


Gauth at a glance


Subjects Math, biology, physics, chemistry and more


Input Photo, typed, voice


Teaching style Answers, voice AI tutor, human experts


Paid price $11.99/month or $99.99/year (US)


### 6. Google Lens Homework Help: Best Free Photo Help


**[Google Lens](https://search.google/ways-to-search/lens/) homework help lets you photograph a question and get "explainers, videos, and results from the web" for "math, history, chemistry, biology, physics, and more."** It is built into the Google app and Google Search, and it absorbed the homework features of the old Socratic by Google app.


Lens is the most accessible tool on this list. It is built into the Google app, so there is nothing extra to buy, and it works on any subject that has good material on the web. Its strength is breadth of explanation: a short video or a well-written explainer often teaches more than a bare solution.


**Pricing:** Lens is part of the Google app. Google's Lens page shows no price for homework help.


**Strengths:**


- Covers almost every school subject, including history
- Points you to explainers and videos, which helps you learn the concept, not only the answer
- Built into the Google app, with no extra subscription


**Watch-outs:** Lens returns what the web has, so quality varies with the source it finds. It does not run a teaching dialogue on its own. For a guided conversation, Google's own answer is Gemini Guided Learning, covered below.


**Skill-safe setting:** Use Lens to find an explainer or a video for the concept behind a problem, not for that exact problem. Watch the explainer, then solve your own problem with the video closed.


Google Lens at a glance


Subjects Math, history, chemistry, biology, physics and more


Input Camera


Teaching style Explainers, videos, web results


Paid price Part of the Google app

## Community and Expert Q&A


These services combine AI answers with human help, from student communities to paid experts. They are strongest for the questions an AI misreads or that need a human to judge.


### 7. Brainly: Best for Community Answers Plus an AI Tutor


**[Brainly](https://brainly.com/) is a learning platform, published by Brainly sp. z o.o., that combines a student community, an AI tutor and test prep, with live human tutors on its top plan.** Its App Store listing pairs the two: "Real human tutors. Smart AI."


Brainly started as a question-and-answer community and has grown into an AI study platform. Students snap a photo or type a question, get step-by-step explanations, and can ask follow-up questions. Its test prep side offers "personalized practice and guided review" from weekly quizzes to final exams, which pushes it toward the practice side of the map.


**Pricing:** The US App Store listing shows Brainly Plus at $9.99 per month or $39.99 per year, and Brainly Tutor at $29.99 per month or $95.99 per year. The same listing shows several other Plus entries at lower prices without explaining the difference, so check the price on your own screen.


**Strengths:**


- A large community, so you can compare more than one explanation
- Test prep and guided review, not only homework answers
- Human tutors on the Tutor plan for students who need a person


**Watch-outs:** Community answers vary in quality, and a copied community answer is still a copied answer. The many price entries make the real cost harder to see before you buy.


**Skill-safe setting:** Use Brainly's test prep and practice for the topics you missed, not the answer feed for the problems you were assigned. If you read a community answer, close it and solve a similar problem from your textbook alone.


Brainly at a glance


Subjects Most school subjects


Input Photo or typed


Teaching style AI tutor, community, human tutors on Tutor plan


Paid price Plus $9.99/month or $39.99/year (US)


### 8. Chegg Study: Best for College Textbook Problems


**[Chegg Study](https://www.chegg.com/) is a subscription study service for college students that offers step-by-step textbook solutions and expert Q&A.** Chegg also owns Mathway, and its textbook library is its main difference from general AI tools.


For a college student in an engineering, accounting or science course that assigns problems from a specific textbook, Chegg's library covers a real gap. A general chatbot does not know which edition and which problem number your professor assigned. Chegg's solutions are organized by textbook, so you can find the worked method that matches your course.


**Pricing:** Chegg's pages did not load for us on November 10, 2026, so we print no price. Third-party reviews quote different figures and question caps. Check the current price on Chegg's subscription page before you subscribe.


**Strengths:**


- Textbook-specific solutions that match college course problem sets
- Expert Q&A for problems that need a human
- Useful for checking a finished problem set against a known method


**Watch-outs:** Chegg's model is solutions-first, which is a risky design for practice. Many universities treat posting graded questions or copying solutions as an academic integrity violation. Read your course policy before you use it on graded work.


**Skill-safe setting:** Use Chegg only after you finish a problem set, to check method on the problems you got wrong. Then redo those problems on a blank page the next day.

## Learning Modes Inside General AI Chatbots


The biggest change in homework help since 2025 is that the major chatbots added learning modes. Each one changes the default from "answer" to "ask," and each one can be switched off by the student.


### 9. ChatGPT Study Mode: Best for Step-by-Step Learning in Any Subject

## The Attempt-First Method: Use AI Without Losing the Skill


**The attempt-first method is a five-step routine that keeps the learning in your head and uses AI only for hints, checks and practice.** It works with every tool on this list, and it takes about five more minutes per problem than copying a solution.


1. **Attempt.** Work the problem for at least 10 minutes on paper, or write one paragraph of your own for an essay. Mark the exact line where you got stuck.
2. **Ask for one hint.** Paste your attempt, not only the problem, and ask for one hint about the next step. The research on failed attempts (Kornell, Hays and Bjork, 2009) says this try is not wasted, even if it was wrong.
3. **Finish the step yourself.** Use the hint, do the next step, and ask for another hint only if you are still stuck.
4. **Explain it back.** When you reach the answer, explain every step in your own words to the AI, and ask it to point out any step you explained wrongly. This is self-explanation and the generation effect at work.
5. **Solve a fresh problem with no AI.** Ask the AI for a new problem of the same type, close the chat, and solve it. Two days later, try one more. That spacing turns a single session into memory.


### Prompts That Keep AI in Coach Mode


The words you type change the help you get. These prompts work in ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Gauth's tutor or a Taskade agent.


```text
HINT, NOT ANSWER
"Here is my attempt: [paste]. I am stuck at line 3.
Give me ONE hint about the next step. Do not solve it."


CHECK MY METHOD
"Here is my finished solution: [paste]. Do not rewrite it.
Tell me which step, if any, has an error, and ask me to fix it."


EXPLAIN-BACK
"I will explain how to solve this in my own words.
Stop me at the first step I explain wrongly and ask a question."


FRESH PRACTICE
"Write 3 new problems like this one, at the same level.
Do not show answers until I send my work."


ESSAY QUESTIONER
"Here is my thesis and outline: [paste]. Do not write any
sentences for me. Ask me 5 questions a skeptical teacher would ask."


```

Explain-back After you reach the answer Self-explanation, generation effect

## How to Grade the AI's Homework


**Grading the AI's homework means checking its answer the way a teacher checks yours: the method, the numbers, the missing pieces and the claims.** This is the skill Loh says everyone now needs, and it is the one skill an answer-only habit never builds.


```text
GRADE THE AI'S HOMEWORK - A 6-POINT CHECK
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. METHOD     Is this the method my class taught?      yes / no
2. NUMBERS    Does a calculator or solver agree?       yes / no
3. UNITS      Are units and signs right at every step?  yes / no
4. MISSING    What did it skip or assume?               list it
5. CLAIMS     Can I find each fact in my textbook?      yes / no
6. EXPLAIN    Can I explain it with the chat closed?    yes / no
Any "no" on 1-3 or 5: the answer is not ready to trust.
A "no" on 6: you have not learned it yet.


```


Language models predict text. They can produce a confident explanation with a wrong step, a made-up quote, or a citation that does not exist. Computational tools such as Wolfram Alpha compute, so they are better checkers for numbers, but they can still answer a different question than the one you meant if the input was misread. Neither replaces the last line of the check.


The deeper skill is metacognition, the ability to judge how well you understand something. Steve Fleming, a cognitive neuroscientist at University College London, measures it as how closely a person's confidence tracks their real performance. Reading a fluent AI explanation raises confidence without raising performance, which is the illusion of explanatory depth in action. Our guide to[what is metacognition](https://www.taskade.com/blog/what-is-metacognition) explains how to train it, and the[Feynman technique](https://www.taskade.com/blog/feynman-technique) is the simplest daily practice for it.

## A Guide for Teachers


**Teachers can turn AI homework helpers from a cheating risk into a coaching tool by writing a clear policy per assignment and grading the reasoning, not only the answer.** Students follow a rule they understand. "No AI" with no reason invites quiet use, while "AI for hints and checks, explain your steps in class" gives a usable line.


Detection software is not a reliable answer. ## Academic Integrity: What Counts as Cheating With AI Homework


**Using AI becomes cheating when you submit AI work as your own, use AI where your teacher banned it, or use it during a test.** Everything else depends on the course policy, which is why the first step is always to read it.


Action Usually allowed? Why


Asking AI to explain a concept from class Yes Same as asking a tutor or reading a textbook


Asking AI to check your finished answer Yes, unless banned You did the work, the AI checks it


Asking AI for practice problems Yes Extra practice is the goal of homework


Asking AI to fix grammar in your draft Depends Some courses count edits as AI use


Pasting AI text or steps into graded work No Misstates who did the work


Paraphrasing AI text to hide it No Rewording does not change authorship


Using AI on a take-home or closed test No, unless allowed Breaks the test rules


Posting graded questions to an answer site No Most schools treat it as a violation


If you are unsure, ask the teacher before you start, and disclose what you used. A disclosed, allowed use protects you. An undisclosed one, even if harmless, looks like hiding.

Is using an AI homework helper cheating?


It depends on what you hand in and on your teacher's rules. Using AI to explain a concept after you tried, to check your own answer, or to make practice questions is usually fine. Copying AI answers or AI-written text into graded work, or using AI during a closed test, is cheating. If your teacher bans AI for an assignment, any use breaks the rule. When the policy asks for it, disclose how you used AI.


Which AI is best for math homework?


Photomath and Mathway are fast for scanning a problem and seeing steps. Symbolab and Wolfram Alpha go deeper into algebra, calculus and statistics, and Wolfram Alpha Pro adds practice problems with hints. Khanmigo and the study modes in ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude are better when you want to be asked questions instead of shown a solution. Attempt the problem first, then use the tool to check your method.


Which AI is best for science homework?


Gauth lists biology, physics and chemistry in its app, and Brainly covers many school subjects with AI explanations and human tutors on paid plans. Google Lens homework help covers chemistry, biology and physics questions with explainers and videos. For understanding a concept, a study mode in ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude that asks you to predict and explain works better than a single answer.


Can AI help with essay homework without writing it for me?


Yes. Ask AI to question your thesis, list counterarguments, explain a grammar rule, or give feedback on a draft you wrote. Keep the drafting, the argument and the final wording yours. Learning modes in ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude are built to ask questions instead of writing for you. Check your teacher's rules, because some courses ban AI feedback on drafts.


Can teachers tell if I used AI for homework?


Not reliably by software. Research shows AI text detectors make errors, and one Stanford study found they often flag essays by non-native English writers as AI-written. Teachers notice other signals: a method that was not taught in class, homework that is much stronger than test results, or a student who cannot explain their own answer. The safest path is to use AI in ways your teacher allows and to disclose it when asked.


What happened to Socratic by Google?


Google retired the standalone Socratic app and moved homework help into Google Lens. The socratic.org site now points to the Lens homework help page. In Lens you can photograph a question in math, history, chemistry, biology or physics and get explainers, videos and web results. Gemini Guided Learning is the Google product that follows the Socratic approach of questions before answers.


Do AI homework helpers make students worse at learning?


They can, when they replace the practice. In a 2025 PNAS study of nearly 1,000 high school students, a plain chatbot raised practice scores by 48 percent but students scored 17 percent lower on a later exam without AI. A tutor version that gave hints instead of answers raised practice scores by 127 percent with no exam loss. The design of the help, and how you use it, decides the result.


Are AI homework apps safe for kids?


Check three things before a child uses one: the minimum age in the terms, what happens to uploaded photos and chats, and whether a parent can see the activity. Khanmigo requires an adult account holder in the United States and lets parents add children. Several homework apps sell trials, special offers and short billing periods, so read the in-app purchase list before you start a trial. For young children, sit with them and use AI as a shared explainer, not a private answer machine.

## The Verdict


**The best AI homework helper is the one you use in the right order: attempt first, then hints, then checks, then fresh practice.** Every tool in this guide can teach, and every tool can also do the exercise for you.
